Modern.brandNameRationale: Picked over Ashmolean Modern (A flagged active institution) and The Enlightenment Hall. A's recommended alt for Ashmolean Modern was 'Ashmole Modern' or 'First Museum' but Cabinet Modern is the cleaner pick — it ties to the Renaissance studiolo / Kunstkammer (the proto-museum of the 16th-17th centuries) without naming any extant institution. The Enlightenment Hall is too close to the British Museum's named gallery. Cabinet Modern is defensibly distinctive and the framing scales (cabinet as a single thematic show, the modern museum as a sequence of cabinets).
Modern.industrySummary: Modern museum branding in 2025+ has moved away from the institutional logo and toward identities that travel across exhibitions, digital, and merchandise. The opening is for a museum brand whose identity flexes per show — the cabinet as the unit of curation and design.
Modern.competitorLandscape: MoMA (moma.org) sets the modern museum identity benchmark. The New Museum (newmuseum.org) plays the contemporary-cabinet slot. Whitechapel (whitechapelgallery.org) holds the London peer position. We sit closest to the New Museum with a tighter cabinet-led framing.
Modern.positioningStatement: A modern museum whose identity is rebuilt for every show.

Luxury.tagline: A private cabinet, opened to members.
Luxury.brandNameRationale: Picked over Studiolo House and Cooper Hewitt Atelier (A flagged Smithsonian conflict). Wunderkammer is the German 'cabinet of curiosities' tradition formalized by Samuel Quiccheberg's 1565 'Inscriptiones' — the original luxury private museum format. Studiolo House is also defensible but Wunderkammer is more globally recognized and the 'Cultural Trust' framing gives the right institutional posture for a members' society. Cooper Hewitt is an active Smithsonian institution and was correctly flagged.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury private museums and members' societies have a real opening — Sir John Soane's Museum, the Frick, the Menil — collectors want curated, intimate institutions over crowded major-museum experiences. The opening is for a Wunderkammer-format private museum and members' society.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Sir John Soane's Museum (soane.org) is the global benchmark for the private collector's museum. The Frick Collection (frick.org) is the New York peer. The Menil Collection (menil.org) plays the Houston modernist-private slot. We sit alongside Soane with a global members' society overlay.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A private museum and members' society in the Wunderkammer tradition.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Picked over Archive. and Hall of Objects. The Cabinet distills the proto-museum format into two words — definite article plus the foundational format. Archive. is clean but archives are a different category (records, papers, not objects). Hall of Objects is more descriptive but loses the cultural-historical weight of the cabinet. The Cabinet is the most defensibly minimal and the most ownable as a museum name.
Minimal.industrySummary: Minimalist museum branding has a real opening for institutions that program a single, focused collection — the customer wants to know what they will see, not what the museum has accumulated. The opening is for a museum brand whose name is the format.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Dia (diaart.org) holds the single-collection minimalist slot. The Roden Crater (rodencrater.com) plays the single-object monumental slot. Donald Judd's Marfa (juddfoundation.org) sits at the same minimalist tier. We sit closer to Judd with a single-focus interior format.
Minimal.positioningStatement: A minimalist museum for a single focused collection.

Corporate.tagline: Collections management for institutions and estates.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Picked over Smithson Institutional Trust (A flagged Smithsonian conflict) and Curatorial Standards Council. Heritage Collections Group is the cleanest B2B framing — 'heritage collection' is the standard professional term, and 'Group' positions the brand as a multi-service operating partner for museums, estates, and institutional holdings. Smithson carries Smithsonian conflict risk even with the 'Trust' variation. Curatorial Standards Council reads more advocacy body than service provider. Heritage Collections Group is defensibly distinctive and clearly B2B.
Corporate.industrySummary: B2B museum services — collections management, conservation, registrar work, deaccession advisory — are fragmented across regional consultancies and large firms (Lunder, Pollard). The opening is for a corporate operating partner serving mid-sized museums, university collections, and private estates.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Lunder Conservation Center (americanart.si.edu/lunder) is the conservation peer. Pollard (pollardarts.com) plays the registrar / collections-management slot. Atelier Art Services (atelierartservices.com) holds the storage and logistics peer position. We sit alongside Pollard with a full-collection-lifecycle service model.
Corporate.positioningStatement: A B2B collections management and conservation partner for museums, university collections, and private estates.

Creative.tagline: An exhibition you can walk through.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Picked over Quiccheberg & Co. and Vitrine & Plinth. Giulio Camillo's 1530s Memory Theatre — a Renaissance proto-museum designed to organize all knowledge spatially — is the perfect anchor for a creative immersive exhibition-design studio. Quiccheberg is academically richer but more theoretical (1565 'Inscriptiones' is a treatise, not a space). Vitrine & Plinth is good but reads more like a furniture company. The Memory Theatre uniquely names the spatial-immersive practice and has an instant visual: a theatre you walk through.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative exhibition-design studios have a real opening in the immersive-experience boom (Meow Wolf, ARTECHOUSE, Hauser & Wirth education programs). The opening is for a studio that brings Renaissance memory-theatre logic to immersive museum and gallery exhibitions.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Local Projects (localprojects.com) is the museum-immersive-design benchmark. Tellart (tellart.com) plays the experience-design peer. ARTECHOUSE (artechouse.com) holds the immersive-museum slot. We sit alongside Local Projects with a Renaissance-rooted memory-theatre methodology.
Creative.positioningStatement: An immersive exhibition-design studio rooted in the Renaissance memory theatre.

targetAudience.primary: Museum directors, gallery directors, and exhibition curators commissioning immersive shows. Values spatial storytelling and design-led curation.

dos: Treat each commission as a single named theatre
Cite Camillo, Quiccheberg, and Yates by name
